findings.evidence: "The branch managers' working group audits renewal rates on the first of every month... Branch-level totals roll up into the consortium's shared reporting dashboard."
findings.fix: Remove this section, or replace it with a summary of circulation data that is actually used to support the recommendation.
findings.violation: This section describes data-collection processes (renewal-rate audits, checkout-volume reviews) that are never referenced again and have no bearing on the fines recommendation, creating a false impression that the recommendation rests on broader circulation analysis than it does.

findings.evidence: "the on-time-or-eventual return rate for borrowed items held at 94 percent"
findings.fix: Report the on-time return rate separately from the eventual-return rate, or revise the later causal claim to match what was actually measured.
findings.violation: The metric conflates on-time returns with eventually-returned-but-late items, so it cannot support the later claim that eliminating fines "increases... on-time return rates" - it only shows items eventually come back, not that they come back by the due date.

findings.evidence: "During a 16-month pilot" ... "The survey was administered at the same pilot branches immediately before and twelve months into the pilot."
findings.fix: Either state the survey's 12-month window consistently wherever the pilot's results are cited, or administer and report a measurement at the pilot's actual end (month 16).
findings.violation: The "after" survey measurement was taken at month 12, not at the end of the 16-month pilot, so the before/after comparison doesn't actually span the full pilot period being cited as evidence.

findings.evidence: "items still unreturned past that window remain subject to the existing replacement-cost billing process, matching the return-rate pattern the pilot data actually established"
findings.fix: Either remove the claim that the 60-day cutoff matches pilot data, or cite the specific return-time distribution data that justifies choosing 60 days.
findings.violation: The pilot data never established any 60-day return-window pattern - the pilot measured only an aggregate return rate (94% vs 87%), not a distribution of return times - so this claim fabricates support that doesn't exist in the data presented.

findings.evidence: "which is the reason the pilot's return-rate and avoidance-survey results, taken together, support ending fines for the whole consortium rather than only the pilot branches"
findings.fix: Provide comparability evidence (e.g., similar patron demographics, circulation volume, or branch size between pilot and non-pilot branches) or soften the claim to acknowledge the extrapolation's uncertainty.
findings.location: "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide" section, first paragraph
findings.violation: This is circular reasoning - it asserts the generalization mechanism as the "reason" the pilot results generalize, without presenting any evidence that the non-pilot branches are comparable to the pilot branches in the relevant respects.

findings.evidence: "This relationship is documented in the Tri-County Library Data Cooperative's 2023 fines-elimination research brief, which reviewed return-rate data from fourteen library systems"
findings.fix: Clarify whether the brief also covers participation/avoidance outcomes, or limit the citation's claimed scope to return-rate findings only.
findings.location: "Why the Pilot Result Applies Systemwide" section, second paragraph
findings.violation: The cited brief is described as covering only return-rate data, yet it's invoked to support the preceding sentence's claim about both return rates and "overall program participation" (the avoidance-survey finding).

findings.evidence: "the four pilot branches absorbed the loss without a measurable change to their replacement-copy spending"
findings.fix: Reconcile the branch count to a single consistent number throughout the document.
findings.violation: This contradicts the earlier statement that the pilot covered "5 branches," creating an unexplained discrepancy in how many branches participated in the pilot.
